types.embedding_query_text: Company: An organization or business entity. Also called organization, firm, corporation. Examples: Meta, Irregular, OpenAI, Anthropic.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are all companies or organizations; Corporation fits the business entity type.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: AIModel: A machine learning model or artificial intelligence system. Also called AI system, neural network, model. Examples: Muse Spark, Meta's Muse Spark model.

chosen_type.label: AIModel
chosen_type.definition: A machine learning model or artificial intelligence system.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an AI model; SoftwareApplication is the closest parent.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: MathSolver
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOutlet: A media organization that reports news. Also called news agency, press, media. Examples: The Information, CNN.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are news outlets; NewsMediaOrganization exactly matches.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: AskPublicNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Also called public appeal article, crowdsourced news request, call for information. Examples: a newspaper asking readers for stories about a local event, a news site requesting photos from a natural disaster, a journalist seeking expert opinions on a topic.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, spokesperson. Examples: Meta spokesperson, source familiar with the situation, spokesperson, the source.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Mentions refer to individuals or roles; Person is the direct match.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A specific day of the week. Also called weekday, day. Examples: Wednesday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'Wednesday' is a specific day; DayOfWeek is the exact enumeration.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A span of time. Also called interval, duration, period. Examples: last week.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'last week' is a span of time; Duration represents a period.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Activity: An action or process. Also called action, operation, task. Examples: cybersecurity testing, evaluations, testing, cyber evals.

chosen_type.label: Action
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are activities; Action is the general type for activities.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: CheckAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

types.embedding_query_text: Resource: A capability or asset that can be accessed or used. Also called asset, access, capability. Examples: internet access, limited internet access, access to the internet.

chosen_type.label: ServiceChannel
chosen_type.justification: Mentions 'internet access' are means to access a service; ServiceChannel fits.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: An intangible entity defining the access rights granted to a specific person or group for a particular digital document. Also called File permission, access control, document rights, sharing setting. Examples: "Read-only access for John Doe", "Edit permission for the Marketing Team", "View and comment access for all users". Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermissionType, which is an enumeration of possible permission types.

candidates.label: Grant
candidates.comment: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: ServiceChannel
candidates.comment: A specific means or method for accessing a service, such as a website, phone number, or physical office. Also called access point, service delivery method, contact channel, customer touchpoint. Examples: a company's customer service hotline, an online booking portal, a government agency's physical office, a mobile app.

types.embedding_query_text: Vulnerability: A weakness in a system that can be exploited. Also called weakness, flaw, security hole. Examples: security vulnerability.

chosen_type.label: MedicalRiskFactor
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'security vulnerability' is a weakness; MedicalRiskFactor is the closest match for vulnerability.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: StructuredValue
candidates.comment: A value for a property that has a complex internal structure rather than being a simple text or reference. Also called complex data type, composite value, structured data. Examples: an address object with street, city, and zip code; a price specification with amount and currency; a time range with start and end times.

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityIncident: An event that compromises security. Also called breach, attack, compromise. Examples: sandbox escape.

chosen_type.label: SecurityIncident
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents a security incident; Event is the parent.

candidates.label: CourseInstance
candidates.comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

candidates.label: UserCheckins
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of checking into a location or event. Also called user check-in, location check-in, event attendance. Examples: a user checking into a restaurant, checking into a concert, marking attendance at a conference.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.

candidates.label: ResetPasswordAction
candidates.comment: ResetPasswordAction is a ControlAction representing the action of resetting the password for a device or application. Also called password recovery, password reset. Examples: resetting an email account password, changing a login password, recovering access to a forgotten account, setting a new device passcode.

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A written or printed work. Also called report, paper, publication. Examples: white paper.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.definition: An event where a report or ranking is published.
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'white paper' is a type of report; Report is the closest match.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: Thesis
candidates.comment: A scholarly document submitted by a candidate for an academic degree or professional qualification. Also called dissertation, academic paper, research thesis. Examples: a PhD dissertation, a master's thesis, an undergraduate honors thesis.

types.embedding_query_text: System: A set of interconnected components or an internal network. Also called network, infrastructure, platform. Examples: internal system.

chosen_type.label: OperatingSystem
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'internal system' likely refers to a computer system; OperatingSystem is the closest.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

types.embedding_query_text: Scenario: A possible situation or set of circumstances. Also called situation, context, case. Examples: real world threat scenarios.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.definition: An event where a record is awarded.
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'real world threat scenarios' are possible situations; Event is the closest general type.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

types.embedding_query_text: CompanyGroup: A category of companies sharing a characteristic. Also called group, set, category. Examples: third major AI company.

chosen_type.label: Consortium
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'third major AI company' refers to a group of companies; Consortium fits a group of organizations.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.
